name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q01 - Plant classification systems and Kingdom Plantae

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding plant classification:

Statement I: Whittaker's (1969) Five Kingdom classification groups living organisms into Monera, Protista, Fungi, Animalia, and Plantae.

Statement II: Fungi and cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are excluded from Kingdom Plantae in the modern view.

Statement III: Linnaeus's artificial system of classification was based mainly on vegetative characters or the androecium structure.

Statement IV: Natural classification systems ignore internal features such as anatomy, ultrastructure, and embryology.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Evaluation of Five Kingdom Classification and Plantae
Whittaker (1969) proposed the Five Kingdom classification comprising Monera, Protista, Fungi, Animalia, and Plantae. Under modern understanding, fungi and cell-walled members of Monera (including cyanobacteria) and Protista are excluded from Plantae.

Step 2: Evaluation of Artificial and Natural Systems
Linnaeus's artificial system was indeed based mainly on vegetative characters or on the androecium structure. In contrast, natural classification systems (such as that of Bentham and Hooker) consider both external features and internal features like ultrastructure, anatomy, embryology, and phytochemistry, so the claim that they ignore internal features is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the first three propositions—concerning Whittaker's Five Kingdoms, exclusion of fungi and cyanobacteria from Plantae, and the basis of Linnaeus's artificial system—are correct (I, II and III only).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q02 - General features and economic importance of algae

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements about algae:

Statement I: Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic, and largely aquatic organisms.

Statement II: At least half of the total carbon dioxide fixation on earth is carried out by algae through photosynthesis.

Statement III: Agar, used to grow microbes and prepare ice-creams and jellies, is obtained from the green alga Chlorella.

Statement IV: Algin is a commercial hydrocolloid obtained from brown algae, whereas carrageen is obtained from red algae.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Evaluation of Algal Nature and Global Photosynthesis
Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic, largely aquatic organisms, and they carry out at least half of the total carbon dioxide fixation on earth through photosynthesis.

Step 2: Evaluation of Commercial Algal Products
Algin is a hydrocolloid obtained from marine brown algae, and carrageen is obtained from marine red algae. However, agar is obtained from the red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria—not from Chlorella (which is a unicellular protein-rich green alga used as a food supplement by space travellers).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the propositions regarding general algal features, global CO₂ fixation, and the sources of algin and carrageen are correct (I, II and IV only).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q03 - Pigments stored food and flagella across algal classes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements comparing the three classes of algae:

Statement I: Chlorophyceae possess chlorophyll a and b and store starch in pyrenoids that contain protein besides starch.

Statement II: Phaeophyceae possess chlorophyll a, c, and fucoxanthin, and store food as laminarin or mannitol.

Statement III: Rhodophyceae possess chlorophyll a, d, and r-phycoerythrin, and store food as floridean starch.

Statement IV: All three algal classes reproduce asexually by biflagellate zoospores with laterally inserted flagella.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Evaluation of Pigments and Stored Food
Chlorophyceae contain chlorophyll a and b and store starch (with pyrenoids containing protein besides starch). Phaeophyceae contain chlorophyll a, c, and fucoxanthin and store laminarin or mannitol. Rhodophyceae contain chlorophyll a, d, and r-phycoerythrin and store floridean starch.

Step 2: Evaluation of Flagellar and Zoospore Characteristics
Flagella are not uniform across all three classes: Chlorophyceae have 2–8 equal, apical flagella; Phaeophyceae have 2 unequal, lateral flagella; and Rhodophyceae completely lack flagella and reproduce asexually by non-motile spores. Thus, the claim about biflagellate lateral zoospores in all three classes is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the first three propositions regarding pigments and stored food in Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, and Rhodophyceae are correct (I, II and III only).

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements about bryophytes:

Statement I: Bryophytes are called amphibians of the plant kingdom because they can live in soil but depend on water for sexual reproduction.

Statement II: The main plant body of a bryophyte is a diploid sporophyte attached to the substratum by true roots.

Statement III: In Marchantia, gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds that develop in gemma cups.

Statement IV: In mosses, the gametophyte consists of a creeping filamentous protonema stage and an upright leafy stage.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Evaluation of Bryophyte Habitat, Gemmae, and Moss Gametophyte
Bryophytes live in soil but depend on water for transfer of antherozoids during sexual reproduction, earning them the title amphibians of the plant kingdom. In Marchantia, gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds formed in gemma cups, and in mosses the gametophyte consists of a creeping filamentous protonema stage followed by an upright leafy stage.

Step 2: Evaluation of Main Plant Body and Attachment
The main plant body of a bryophyte is a haploid gametophyte (not a diploid sporophyte), and it lacks true roots, stems, or leaves, being attached to the substratum by unicellular or multicellular rhizoids. Thus, the claim of a diploid sporophyte with true roots is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the propositions regarding amphibian nature, gemmae in Marchantia, and the two gametophyte stages in mosses are correct (I, III and IV only).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q05 - Vascular tissues sporophyte prothallus and heterospory in pteridophytes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements about pteridophytes:

Statement I: Evolutionarily, pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues—xylem and phloem.

Statement II: The main plant body is a sporophyte differentiated into true root, stem, and leaves.

Statement III: The prothallus is an inconspicuous, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte requiring cool, damp, shady places.

Statement IV: All pteridophytes are strictly homosporous without any heterosporous genera.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Evaluation of Pteridophyte Vascularity, Sporophyte, and Prothallus
Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants with xylem and phloem; their main plant body is a sporophyte with true roots, stems, and leaves, and their spores germinate into a small, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte (prothallus) requiring cool, damp, shady places.

Step 2: Evaluation of Spore Types
While the majority of pteridophytes are homosporous, genera such as Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores (macro and micro spores) and are heterosporous. Thus, the claim that all pteridophytes are strictly homosporous is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the propositions regarding vascular tissues, dominant sporophyte with true organs, and prothallus requirements are correct (I, II and III only).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q06 - Gymnosperm ovules roots leaves and gametophytes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements about gymnosperms:

Statement I: Ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall, so the seeds that develop post-fertilisation remain naked.

Statement II: Pinus has mycorrhizal roots and branched stems, whereas Cycas has coralloid roots with N₂-fixing cyanobacteria and unbranched stems.

Statement III: Male and female gametophytes in gymnosperms have an independent, free-living existence.

Statement IV: In conifers, needle-like leaves, a thick cuticle, and sunken stomata help reduce water loss.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Evaluation of Ovules, Roots, Stems, and Leaf Adaptations
Gymnosperms have exposed ovules and naked seeds; Pinus has mycorrhiza and branched stems while Cycas has coralloid roots with N₂-fixing cyanobacteria and unbranched stems; and conifer leaves have needle-like form, thick cuticle, and sunken stomata to reduce water loss.

Step 2: Evaluation of Gametophyte Independence
Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, gymnosperm male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence—they remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes. Thus, the claim of independent free-living gametophytes is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the propositions regarding naked ovules/seeds, root and stem differences in Pinus and Cycas, and xerophytic leaf adaptations in conifers are correct (I, II and IV only).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q07 - Angiosperm floral organs embryo sac and double fertilisation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements about angiosperms:

Statement I: The male sex organ in a flower is the stamen (filament and anther) and the female sex organ is the pistil (ovary, style, and stigma).

Statement II: Each embryo sac has a three-celled egg apparatus (one egg cell and two synergids), three antipodal cells, and two polar nuclei.

Statement III: Double fertilisation involves syngamy (forming a diploid zygote) and triple fusion (forming a triploid primary endosperm nucleus).

Statement IV: After fertilisation, synergids and antipodals persist to nourish the embryo, while the ovary develops into the seed.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Evaluation of Floral Organs, Embryo Sac, and Double Fertilisation
In angiosperms, the stamen and pistil are the male and female sex organs respectively; the embryo sac has a three-celled egg apparatus (egg cell + two synergids), three antipodals, and two polar nuclei; and double fertilisation comprises syngamy (zygote) and triple fusion (triploid PEN).

Step 2: Evaluation of Post-Fertilisation Fate
After fertilisation, synergids and antipodals degenerate (while PEN forms endosperm to nourish the embryo), ovules develop into seeds, and the ovary develops into the fruit. Hence, the post-fertilisation claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the first three propositions regarding floral sex organs, embryo sac organisation, and double fertilisation are correct (I, II and III only).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTKINGDOM_MCQ_Q08 - Synthesis of plant life cycles and ploidy

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding plant life cycles and ploidy:

Statement I: Volvox and Spirogyra are haplontic, Fucus is diplontic, and Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, and kelps are haplo-diplontic.

Statement II: Both bryophytes and pteridophytes exhibit a haplo-diplontic life cycle, with a dominant gametophyte in bryophytes and a dominant sporophyte in pteridophytes.

Statement III: All seed-bearing plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms) follow a diplontic life cycle pattern with some variations.

Statement IV: A moss protonemal cell, a fern prothallus cell, and a Marchantia gemma cell are all haploid (n), whereas a dicot primary endosperm nucleus is triploid (3n).

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Evaluation of Life Cycle Patterns Across Plant Groups
Most algae like Volvox and Spirogyra are haplontic, whereas Fucus is diplontic and Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, and kelps are haplo-diplontic. All bryophytes and pteridophytes are haplo-diplontic (with dominant gametophyte in bryophytes and dominant sporophyte in pteridophytes), and all seed plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms) follow a diplontic pattern.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ploidy Levels
The protonemal cell of a moss, prothallus cell of a fern, and gemma cell of Marchantia are all gametophytic/asexual haploid structures (n), whereas the dicot primary endosperm nucleus formed by triple fusion is triploid (3n).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
All four propositions regarding algal life cycles, bryophyte/pteridophyte haplo-diplontic cycles, seed plant diplontic cycles, and cellular ploidy levels are correct (I, II, III and IV).
